data.narrative:
Ouros Energy is a seed-stage climate and energy company founded by Ethan Loosbrock that has raised $3M+ to date. The valuation universe comprises nine private peers in the climate and energy sector, including later-stage companies such as Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen, alongside one public comparable (LNZA).

A stage-progression analysis applies a 2.5x multiplier to the $3M raised proxy, which is standard for seed-to-next-stage transitions in venture. This method yields an implied valuation of $8M. A peer-median approach could not be applied: while nine same-sector peers exist, none of the narrower filters—same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier—produced the minimum three datapoints required for statistical reliability. Applying an all-sector median would introduce material bias given the heterogeneity of climate and energy subsectors and development stages.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $6M to $9M, with a median of $8M. This estimate rests on a single triangulation method, introducing meaningful uncertainty. Key limitations include the absence of direct seed-stage comparables in the narrow peer set and reliance on the stage-progression multiplier as a standalone anchor. Resolution of these uncertainties would require either identifying additional seed-stage climate and energy peers or gathering forward-looking metrics (burn rate, customer traction) that might inform alternative methodologies.
